memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"He said, 'If you listen carefully to the LORD your God and do what is right in
his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his decrees, I will
not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians, for I am the
LORD, who heals you.'" - Ex 15:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God gives Himself a name: the LORD who heals you.

We must handle this verse carefully, because it is often misused. This is a
covenant word spoken to Israel at a specific moment, contrasting them with Egypt
under judgment. It is not a blanket guarantee that obedient Christians will never
be ill. Scripture will not support that. Paul left Trophimus sick at Miletus
(2 Tim 4:20). Timothy had frequent stomach trouble (1 Tim 5:23). Paul himself
carried a thorn God chose not to remove (2 Cor 12:8-9). Faithful people get sick,
and it is cruel to suggest otherwise.

What does not change is the name. God is the healer. Every recovery, whether
through medicine, rest, time, or direct intervention, comes from Him.

Notice also the connection God draws between obedience and wellbeing. There is
real wisdom here that we should not dismiss. Much human suffering does flow from
ignoring God's ways. But Job stands in Scripture precisely to stop us concluding
that every illness is a verdict on someone's obedience.

So we pray boldly for healing, we thank God for doctors, and we hold outcomes
with open hands. He is the LORD who heals, in His way and His timing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you thank God for healing that came through ordinary means?
2. Have you ever assumed sickness meant someone had failed God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are the God who heals. I bring my body and my loved ones to You, and I
trust You with the outcome. Amen.
